topics.title: Design a URL Shortener
topics.description: Understanding large-scale URL shortening systems including hashing strategies, caching, database design, and redirect flows.

subtopics.title: Problem Overview
subtopics.theory:
1️⃣ Problem Overview

Interview Definition

A URL shortener is a system that converts a long URL into a short, unique alias and redirects users from the short URL to the original URL efficiently at large scale.



Core Use Cases

URL Shortening

URL Redirecting

High availability

Scalability

subtopics.title: Back-of-the-Envelope Estimation
subtopics.theory:
2️⃣ Back-of-the-Envelope Estimation

Interview Definition

Back-of-the-envelope estimation is a rough calculation used to validate system feasibility and scale.



Important Points

100M URLs/day

~365B URLs in 10 years

62 characters allowed (0-9, a-z, A-Z)

7 characters enough (62⁷ ≈ 3.5T)



Advantages

Prevents under-designing

Helps choose hash length

Validates scalability

Disadvantages

Approximate numbers only

Depends on assumptions

subtopics.title: API Design
subtopics.theory:
3️⃣ API Design

Interview Definition

API design defines how clients interact with the URL shortening system using REST endpoints.



Important Points

POST /shorten → Create short URL

GET /{shortURL} → Redirect

Use HTTP 301 redirect

Stateless APIs



Advantages

Clean separation of responsibilities

Easy scaling

Cache-friendly

Disadvantages

Needs proper versioning

Must handle invalid URLs

subtopics.title: Data Model
subtopics.theory:
4️⃣ Data Model

Interview Definition

The data model defines how URL mappings are stored persistently for scalability and reliability.



Table Design

id

short_url

long_url



Important Points

id is BIGINT primary key

short_url indexed

long_url stored as text

Append-only system



Advantages

Simple schema

Easy indexing

Strong consistency

Disadvantages

Storage grows continuously

Requires sharding at scale

subtopics.title: Hash Function Design
subtopics.theory:
5️⃣ Hash Function Design

Interview Definition

A hash function converts long URLs into short identifiers while ensuring uniqueness and scalability.



Two Approaches

1. Hash + Collision Resolution

Use MD5/SHA

Handle collisions manually

Advantage

Simple concept

Disadvantage

Collisions possible

Multiple DB checks



2. Base-62 Conversion (Preferred)

Convert unique numeric ID → Base-62 string.

Example:

2009215674938 → zn9edcu



Advantages

No collisions

Faster

Deterministic

Disadvantages

Requires distributed ID generator

subtopics.title: URL Shortening Flow
subtopics.theory:
6️⃣ URL Shortening Flow

Interview Definition

The URL shortening flow generates a unique ID, converts it to a short code, stores it, and returns the short URL.



Flow

Receive long URL

Check duplicate

Generate unique ID

Convert to Base-62

Store in DB

Return short URL



Advantages

Collision-free

Simple logic

Scalable

Disadvantages

DB write required

Requires ID coordination

subtopics.title: URL Redirecting Flow
subtopics.theory:
7️⃣ URL Redirecting Flow

Interview Definition

The redirecting flow retrieves the original URL using a cache-first strategy and returns an HTTP redirect response.



Flow

User clicks short URL

Load balancer routes request

Check cache

If miss → check DB

Return 301 redirect



Advantages

Very fast with cache

DB load reduced

Disadvantages

Cache consistency issues

Requires proper TTL management

subtopics.title: Caching Strategy
subtopics.theory:
8️⃣ Caching Strategy

Interview Definition

Caching stores frequently accessed URL mappings in memory to reduce latency and database load.



Important Concepts

Cache-aside pattern

LRU eviction

TTL

DB as source of truth



Advantages

Millisecond response time

Scales reads easily

Reduces DB pressure

Disadvantages

Stale data risk

Extra memory cost

subtopics.title: Additional Design Considerations
subtopics.theory:
9️⃣ Additional Design Considerations

Rate Limiting

Limits URL creation requests per user/IP.

Database Replication

Primary handles writes, replicas handle reads.

Sharding

Split database across servers for scalability.

Analytics

Track click counts and usage.

Availability

No single point of failure.

subtopics.title: Important Definitions
subtopics.theory:
🔑 Important Definitions (Interview Words)

Unique ID Generator

A distributed system component that generates globally unique numeric IDs.

Base-62 Encoding

A numbering system using 62 characters to shorten numeric IDs.

Cache-Aside

Application checks cache first, then database if miss.

TTL (Time To Live)

Time duration before cached data expires.

Sharding

Horizontal partitioning of database across multiple machines.

Replication

Copying data across servers for availability.

Stateless Server

Server that does not store session locally.

301 Redirect

Permanent HTTP redirect response.

subtopics.title: Final Summary
subtopics.theory:
🎯 Final One-Line Summary

A URL shortener uses a unique ID generator with Base-62 encoding, a simple relational data model, and a cache-first redirect strategy to serve billions of URL requests efficiently and reliably.
